dishes.name: Aligot
dishes.desc: Mashed potato whipped with fresh Laguiole tomme, butter and garlic until it stretches in ribbons. The best-known Aveyron dish, served on the Aubrac plateau and in Rodez.

dishes.name: Farçous
dishes.desc: Fried savoury fritters of chard, herbs and sometimes pork, a traditional Aveyron farm dish. Sold in bakeries and markets around Rodez.

dishes.name: Tripoux
dishes.desc: Small parcels of sheep tripe and feet, stuffed and simmered in white wine and tomato. A rustic Aveyron speciality served in local restaurants.

dishes.name: Fouace
dishes.desc: Orange-blossom brioche shaped as a crown, traditional in Aveyron bakeries. Eaten at celebrations and as an everyday pastry.

dishes.name: Estofinado
dishes.desc: Dried cod mashed with potato, cream, garlic and walnut oil. A dish of Rodez and the Aveyron valleys, found in traditional restaurants.

dishes.name: Roquefort
dishes.desc: Blue ewe's-milk cheese ripened in the natural caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in south Aveyron. A regional cheese found on every local cheese board.
